newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: HARMONY SEEKS TO INCREASE DIRECT GOLD SALES.
newsitem.headline: HARMONY SEEKS TO INCREASE DIRECT GOLD SALES.

text.p: Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd will seek permission from South Africa's central Reserve Bank to market more than the current third of its gold direct, managing director Bernard Swanepoel said on Monday.
Harmony received Reserve Bank permission earlier this year to market internationally a third of its gold output.
South Africa's Rand Refinery -- the world's biggest which is collectively owned by the gold mining industry -- has said that it already markets gold direct on behalf of producers.
But Swanepoel said at the company's results presentation that Harmony would attempt to get permission to sell more than a third of its gold output of around 24 tonnes.
"We will certainly pursue the matter and try and sell more than that," he said.

Currently all South African gold mines refine their gold at the Rand Refinery but Harmony announced last year that it will break ranks by establishing its own commercial-scale refinery which should be completed in the third quarter of 1997.
